# Prodigo for OpenCode

**By Northwiser LLC** · Product support: **info@prodigo.ai** · Company contact:
**info@northwiser.ai**. Package identity: `@northwiser/opencode-prodigo`.
This checkout is a prerelease candidate; building it does not publish it.

Interactive **Prodigo onboarding** for OpenCode V2: sign-in, approved Pega
target selection, Pega connection selection and background rule fetches, all
through the local Prodigo Core service — the terminal counterpart of the
orkaid VSIX commands.

**Status: experimental.** The full journey (sign-in → target → connection →
apps → rulesets → fetch → progress → result, plus restart recovery) has run on
a real OpenCode 2.2.6 host against loopback stand-ins for the Portal and Core
that follow the Core contract (`rust/orkdmcp`, connection onboarding
architecture doc). It has **not** yet run against a live Core with a real Pega
target, and the dialogs have not been exercised by a person. See
[measured results](https://github.com/jgasmi/pega-local-router/blob/main/docs/measured-results.md).

## Commands

One slash command: **`/prodigo`** (alias `/pega`) opens the menu:

| Menu entry | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Sign in to Prodigo | Validate a Prodigo API token against the Portal and store it privately (or use `tokenEnv`). The first time, it also asks where fetched rules should be saved |
| Select Pega target | Searchable list of approved targets with env and restricted/blocked badges; then offers the Pega connection step |
| Connect Pega operator | Reuse a connection the Core service already holds for this target (no password), or enroll a new operator once; offers the one-time trust setup when Core asks for it |
| Fetch rules | Application → rulesets (with rule counts, or all) → keep / replace / skip (remembered per app) → confirm. Core downloads and parses in the background into your rules folder; progress appears as toasts and the result as a dialog |
| Set rules folder | Choose or change where fetched rules are saved |
| Stop following fetch | Shown while a fetch runs. Core has no cancel endpoint, so the job finishes in the background; this only stops progress updates |
| Show status | Session, target, connection, Core URL, MCP and fetch state |
| Sign out | Clear the stored token and selection (Core keeps enrolled connections) |

Each entry is also a command-palette command ("Prodigo: …").

## How it works

- **Core owns Pega access.** A Pega password is sent exactly once, to the
  loopback Core service at enrollment (`POST /service/connections`); Core
  verifies it and keeps it in the OS credential store. Afterwards everything is
  selected by connection *name*, so a restart needs no password. The plugin
  never calls Pega itself.
- **Fetch is the VSIX fetch.** `POST /rules/dry-run` in async mode with the same
  rule types as the VSIX, observed over `/runs/{id}/stream`; Core writes the XML
  and the parsed JSON corpus.
- **MCP selection follows the connection.** Once a connection is ready, the MCP
  entry named by `mcp.server` gets `X-Prodigo-Connection: <name>`, and an
  existing `?connection=` URL parameter is rewritten to the same name (Core
  rejects a mismatch). With nothing selected the entry is left exactly as you
  wrote it. Config files are never edited and MCP servers are never created.
- **Rules folder:** always named `prodigo-output`. You choose *where* at first
  sign-in (or at the first fetch): entering `~/devcenter` gives
  `~/devcenter/prodigo-output`; a path already ending in `prodigo-output` is
  kept. The choice is remembered across restarts and sign-out, wherever
  OpenCode is started. Nothing is fetched until it is chosen; a full path is
  required. When OpenCode runs in a project, the prompt suggests
  `<project>/prodigo-output`. A `fetch.outputRoot` in config overrides the
  saved choice and is used exactly as written.
- **Core URL:** `core.baseUrl` if set, else the origin of the MCP entry's URL,
  else `http://127.0.0.1:8700`. Only plain loopback HTTP is ever used.

## Install (isolated test first)

Release automation compiles and checks an npm tarball on GitHub (Linux/macOS).
See [packaging and release instructions](https://github.com/jgasmi/pega-local-router/blob/main/docs/prodigo-releasing.md).
After npm publication, replace the local package path with the pinned
`@northwiser/opencode-prodigo@<version>`; do not load both copies.

Merge from [config.example.jsonc](config.example.jsonc) into a **separate test
location's** `opencode.jsonc`; keep your existing providers, MCP servers and
permissions. Point `mcp.server` at the key of your Prodigo MCP entry. The
package provides the server part (`.`), the terminal dialogs (`./tui`) and the
RPC contract (`./rpc`).

## Threat model (honest version)

- The Prodigo token is stored **unencrypted** at `0600` in
  `~/.local/state/opencode-prodigo/` (configurable). OS keychain storage is
  tracked (#9). `tokenEnv` avoids disk entirely.
- Token and password prompts are **not masked**: the stock OpenCode prompt has
  no secret mode, and an earlier custom dialog did not work (tracked in #7).
  Enter them where nobody watches the screen.
- The Pega password is held only for the single enrollment request and is never
  persisted, logged or returned by any RPC method.
- Target selection is validated live against the Portal bootstrap on every
  call; blocked and unknown URLs are refused. Credentials only go to a loopback
  HTTP origin, never to a caller-selected host.
- **Pega writes:** the plugin performs none itself. The optional, explicitly
  confirmed *trust setup* makes Core install Prodigo's trust policy in Pega and
  requires an authorized Pega administrator. Fetching only reads Pega.
- Local writes happen only inside the fetch output root, and Core does them.
- The plugin adds no tool surface to the model.

# Changelog — Prodigo for OpenCode

## 0.1.0-beta.1

First packaged beta candidate (not published merely by building this package).

- One `/prodigo` menu for sign-in, target and Core connection selection.
- Background Core rule-fetch jobs, progress and explicit trust setup approval.
- A remembered, user-selected location for `prodigo-output`.
- Compiled server, TUI and RPC exports under `@northwiser/opencode-prodigo`.

Known limitations: visible secret prompts, plaintext restricted-permission
token storage, one-or-all ruleset selection, and detach rather than true Core
job cancellation. See SECURITY.md and README.md before rollout.

# Security — Prodigo for OpenCode

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to **info@prodigo.ai**. Company
contact: **info@northwiser.ai** (Northwiser LLC).

Do not include tokens, Pega passwords, customer rule data or sensitive hosts
in public issues. Send a minimal, sanitized reproduction, the plugin version,
OpenCode version and operating system. We do not promise a response SLA.

## Support status

The plugin is prerelease software; there is no stable supported release yet.
Use the newest published beta for security fixes. Server loading has been
exercised on OpenCode 2.2.6 with SDK 2.2.7, not on every OpenCode release.

Token and password prompts are currently visible. The plugin's token store
is unencrypted with restricted file permissions. Pega credentials are enrolled
with loopback Prodigo Core; fetched data stays local. See README.md for the
full limitations and trust-initialization approval boundary.
